# Baghdad 830 – Computing, control & information theory

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Algorithm (exact step-by-step procedure)** [`algorithm_concept`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/algorithm_concept.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Al-Khwarizmi's arithmetic and algebra teach fixed procedures in words; his Latinised name will become 'algorithm'. Euclid's procedures and Indian astronomical rules (kuttaka) are known. Inheritance shares under Islamic law are a mass market for exact procedures. Local: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi; qadis and inheritance calculators (fara'id).
- **Binary numbers** [`binary_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/binary_numbers.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Doubling and halving (tad'if, tansif) are standard steps in Indian and Arabic reckoning, the seed of binary. Pingala's metres and the I Ching are out of sight.
- **Boolean logic (algebra of true and false)** [`boolean_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boolean_logic.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle's Categories, On Interpretation and Prior Analytics circulate in Syriac and early Arabic; Christian and Muslim theologians argue with syllogisms in court debates. No algebra of propositions. Local: Nestorian scholars teaching the Organon; court debates (majalis) before al-Ma'mun.
- **Switching circuits and logic gates** [`logic_gates_switching`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/logic_gates_switching.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Mechanical calculator** [`mechanical_calculator`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_calculator.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. The astrolabe is an analogue computer in brass, and its makers cut fine scales. Geared calculators of the Antikythera kind are unknown; an equatorium is centuries away. Local: Ali ibn Isa al-Asturlabi.
- **Punched cards for control and data** [`punched_card_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/punched_card_control.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Silk drawlooms in the royal tiraz workshops store patterns in cords pulled by a draw-boy. Nobody sees the store as information. Local: tiraz workshops (inscribed textiles for the court); silk weavers of Tustar and Baghdad.
- **Programmable computer (stored program)** [`programmable_computer`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/programmable_computer.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. The Banu Musa, now young men, will build automata with a pinned drum that can be re-pegged for a new tune (c. 850). That is as close as this world comes. Local: the Banu Musa brothers.

- **Information theory (bit, entropy, channel capacity)** [`information_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/information_theory.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Grammarians count letter frequencies and the combinations of roots (al-Khalil's dictionary counted possible roots); this is where a statistical view of text could start. Local: al-Khalil's Kitab al-Ayn (combinatorics of Arabic roots).

- **Error-detecting and error-correcting codes** [`error_correcting_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/error_correcting_codes.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Copyists collate manuscripts and hadith scholars check chains of transmitters; both are error-control practices. Check sums on numbers (casting out nines) arrive with Indian arithmetic. Local: hadith transmitters (isnad criticism); Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (Indian reckoning).

Float valves of Ctesibius and Hero are in Greek books; the Banu Musa will build float regulators and automatic lamps (c. 850). Water clocks and fountains already use simple levels. Local: the Banu Musa brothers.
- **Cryptography and codebreaking (ciphers, frequency analysis, one-time pad)** [`cryptography`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cryptography.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Secretaries and the barid use letter substitutions and code words; grammarians count letters. Al-Kindi will write the first treatise on breaking ciphers by letter frequency, date uncertain, probably later in his life. Local: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi; chancery secretaries (kuttab); postmasters of the barid.
